name: backup
summary: take an etcd snapshot now, list the snapshots, download one, or decrypt one on this machine
description:
etcd snapshots are taken by the operator, on the schedule an EtcdBackupPolicy
sets, and kept encrypted to the age public keys the policy names. The operator
holds no private key: it can store a snapshot but not read one. Decrypting
needs one of the matching age identities, on your own machine.

Restoring is pk-metal restore; https://metal.platform-kit.org/operate/day-2/restore-etcd/ walks through it.

subcommands.name: now
subcommands.summary: take a snapshot now (it waits until stored; --wait=false returns at once)

flags.name: wait
flags.usage: wait until the snapshot is stored and verified

subcommands.name: list
subcommands.summary: list the snapshots, newest first; RECIPIENTS shows the last 8 characters of each age public key a snapshot is encrypted to (compare with: age-keygen -y <identity file>)

subcommands.name: get
subcommands.summary: download the encrypted snapshot (s3 sinks; pvc sinks: see the message)

flags.name: to-file
flags.usage: file to write the encrypted snapshot to (required; it must not exist)

subcommands.name: decrypt
subcommands.summary: decrypt on this machine and check it is an intact etcd snapshot; with --plaintext-file, also write the plaintext (it holds every Secret of the cluster)

flags.name: identity
flags.usage: age identity file (required): the secret key, as age-keygen writes it

flags.name: in
flags.usage: decrypt this file instead of downloading the snapshot

flags.name: plaintext-file
flags.usage: also write the plaintext snapshot here (mode 0600; it must not exist)
